primary_claim: In layer 12 of Gemma-2-2B, most residual-stream directions lose predictive signal within a single token, but a compact ~31-dimensional subspace has much longer autocorrelation timescales (90th percentile 17 tokens vs 1 for random/PCA directions); this slow subspace accounts for essentially all cross-token persistence (projecting it out collapses held-out timescale to near-null), depends on sequential token order rather than token composition alone, and aligns with attention-output geometry more than chance.

effect.value: 17 tokens for time-lagged probes vs 1 token for random/PCA directions

stated_future_work: use a corpus that forces the held-state vs live-variable distinction (multi-step proofs, long-horizon code, controlled reasoning tasks with labeled running variable)
add sentence-level shuffling and paraphrase controls to cut local lexical clustering
build a direct held vs. live discriminator by regressing slow-direction projections against labeled quantities
test whether a steering vector shifts maintained state or just 'greases the logits'
test whether features decompose into fast and slow components
test whether sparse-feature methods could be constrained to the high-timescale region
limitations_stated: single corpus (C4), single layer (12), single model (Gemma-2-2B) used, so no broad interpretability claims are licensed
semantic readout of what slow directions encode is exploratory, not a locked quantitative result; only ten samples per span family inspected, on validation only
labels for what slow directions encode are coarse regex summaries, not trained classifiers or validated semantic variables
500-direction subspace battery supports claims about generic directions but not a proof that every direction in the continuous span is slow
test split had been inspected elsewhere in the workflow before the battery classification rule was locked, so test results are formally exploratory
quote: most residual directions are fast, as their projected values stop being predictive after just one token. But a small set of directions is much slower.
